column2: Large Language Models for Supply Chain Optimization
column3: Beibin Li; Konstantina Mellou; Bo Zhang; Jeevan Pathuri; Ishai Menache
column8: Proposes an LLM-mediated interface (OptiGuide) over combinatorial optimization to answer what-if questions and explain optimization outcomes, targeting interpretability and trust in decision support.

column2: Hybrid LLM/Rule-based Approaches to Business Insights Generation from Structured Data
column8: Explores hybrid LLM + rule-based systems for generating actionable BI insights from structured data, relevant to grounding, controllability, and reducing hallucinations in enterprise analytics.

Barrere; Shelley Evenson; Rahul Basole; Connie Miao; Ankit Mehta; Fabien Boulay; Su Min Park; Natalie E. Pearson; Eldhose Joy; Tiger He; Sumiran Thakur; Koustav Ghosal; Josh On; Phoebe Morrison; Tim Major; Eva Siqi Wang; Gina Escobar; Jiaheng Wei; Tharindu Cyril Weerasooriya; Queena Song; Daria Lashkevich; Clare Chen; Gyuhak Kim; Dengpan Yin; Don Hejna; Mo Nomeli; Wei Wei
column8: Introduces a domain-focused LLM system for business/media analytics; useful as an example of enterprise retrieval/curation patterns and evaluation considerations for reliable insight generation.

column2: AI Agents-as-Judge: Automated Assessment of Accuracy, Consistency, Completeness and Clarity for Enterprise Documents
column8: Evaluates agentic LLMs as automated “judges” for enterprise documents along multiple quality axes, informing Phase 2 evaluation design (accuracy/consistency/completeness/clarity).

column2: Enhancing Business Analytics through Hybrid Summarization of Financial Reports
column8: Presents hybrid extractive–abstractive financial summarization with an emphasis on factual reliability, providing techniques and metrics relevant to faithfulness-focused generation.

column2: The Dark Side of AI Transformers: Sentiment Polarization & the Loss of Business Neutrality by NLP Transformers
column8: Discusses risks of transformer-based NLP in sentiment/business settings (e.g., polarization/neutrality issues), motivating governance and trust constraints in enterprise deployments.

column2: Can LLMs Clean Up Your Mess? A Survey of Application-Ready Data Preparation with LLMs
column3: Wei Zhou; Jun Zhou; Haoyu Wang; Zhenghao Li; Qikang He; Shaokun Han; Guoliang Li; Xuanhe Zhou; Yeye He; Chunwei Liu; Zirui Tang; Bin Wang; Shen Tang; Kai Zuo; Yuyu Luo; Zhenzhe Zheng; Conghui He; Jingren Zhou; Fan Wu
column8: Survey of LLM-supported data preparation (cleaning, integration, profiling, labeling), directly relevant to building/maintaining your RAG corpus and ensuring reproducible ingestion pipelines.

column2: Harnessing Large Language Models for Precision Querying and Retrieval-Augmented Knowledge Extraction in Clinical Data Science
column3: Juan Jose Rubio Jan; Jack Wu; Julia Ive
column8: Applies LLMs to structured querying and a RAG pipeline for clinical text extraction, offering a close analog to your Phase 2 baseline (retrieval, extraction, and evaluation).

column2: CARE-RFT: Confidence-Anchored Reinforcement Finetuning for Reliable Reasoning in Large Language Models
column3: Shuozhe Li; Jincheng Cao; Bodun Hu; Aryan Mokhtari; Leqi Liu; Amy Zhang
column8: Studies the trade-off between reasoning gains and trustworthiness under reinforcement finetuning and proposes confidence-anchored regularization, informing reliability and calibration discussions.

column2: LLMs as High-Dimensional Nonlinear Autoregressive Models with Attention: Training, Alignment and Inference
column8: Provides an equation-level mathematical framing of LLM training/alignment/inference, useful for grounding system design choices and failure analysis in a formal perspective.

column2: Hallucination is a Consequence of Space-Optimality: A Rate-Distortion Theorem for Membership Testing
column8: Develops a theoretical account linking hallucination on “random facts” to memory-efficiency limits, helping explain why some ungrounded errors persist even with better prompting.

column2: From Sycophancy to Sensemaking: Premise Governance for Human–AI Decision Making
column3: Raunak Jain; Mudita Khurana; John Stephens; Srinivas Dharmasanam; Shankar Venkataraman
column8: Proposes “premise governance” to reduce sycophancy and support auditable decisions, aligning with traceability + trust behaviors you’ll need in RAG.

column2: Prototype Transformer: Towards Language Model Architectures Interpretable by Design
column3: Yordan Yordanov; Matteo Forasassi; Bayar Menzat; Ruizhi Wang; Chang Qi; Markus Kaltenberger; Amine M’Charrak; Tommaso Salvatori; Thomas Lukasiewicz
column8: Introduces a self-attention alternative using prototypes to improve interpretability and robustness analysis, relevant to understanding/mitigating opaque failure modes such as hallucination.

column2: Olmix: A Framework for Data Mixing Throughout LM Development
column3: Mayee F. Chen; Tyler Murray; David Heineman; Matt Jordan; Hannaneh Hajishirzi; Christopher Ré; Luca Soldaini; Kyle Lo
column8: Studies practical data-mixing design choices and domain-set evolution during LM development, offering patterns for corpus curation decisions and reproducible dataset management.

column2: HalluClean: A Unified Framework to Combat Hallucinations in LLMs
column8: Proposes a task-agnostic, prompt-based detect-and-revise pipeline (planning/execution/revision) to reduce hallucinated content without external knowledge, directly relevant to hallucination mitigation.

column2: Intelligent Identification and Decision Support System for TBM Construction Risk Synergistically Driven by Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models
column8: Example of combining a knowledge graph with an LLM for risk identification/decision support, illustrating how structured knowledge can constrain generation and reduce hallucination in a domain system.
